lessons.title: Handling Inquiries and Converting Leads to Clients
lessons.body: When a potential client calls or WhatsApps you, they are shopping around. In Africa, most inquiries come via WhatsApp, phone calls, or referrals. You must respond within 5 minutes during business hours. If you delay, they will call the next cleaner. Keep a simple script: greet them warmly, ask for their location, type of space (home or office), size (number of rooms or square meters), and when they need cleaning. For example: 'Hello, thank you for contacting Sparkle Clean. May I know your location and the size of the space?' Write down their answers in a notebook or a free app like Google Sheets. Then give a rough estimate on the spot if possible, but always say you need to see the space for a final quote. If they hesitate, offer a 10% discount for first-time clients. Follow up within 24 hours with a WhatsApp message summarizing what you discussed and a proposed time for a site visit. Track your leads: for every 10 inquiries, aim to convert 3 to 4 into site visits, and 2 to 3 into paying clients. Use a simple CRM like HubSpot CRM (free) or a notebook with columns: Name, Contact, Date, Status. Never let a lead go coldâsend a friendly reminder after 3 days. Remember, people buy from those they trust, so be polite, professional, and prompt.

lessons.title: Conducting On-Site Estimates and Walkthroughs
lessons.body: An on-site estimate is your chance to win the job. Arrive on time, dressed neatly, with a clipboard, measuring tape, and a smartphone for photos. Walk through the space with the client. Note the number of rooms, type of flooring (tiles, carpet, wood), windows, bathrooms, kitchen, and any special areas like carpets or upholstery. Measure the total square metersâfor example, a 3-bedroom apartment in Nairobi might be 120 square meters. Ask about frequency: daily, weekly, or one-time. For offices, ask about number of desks, restrooms, and kitchenettes. Take photos of problem areas like stained carpets or dusty blinds. While walking, explain your process: 'We use eco-friendly detergents, and for carpets we use a machine that extracts dirt.' Give a verbal estimate at the end: for a 120 sqm home, a deep clean might cost KES 5,000 to 8,000. For a 200 sqm office, weekly cleaning might be KES 15,000 per month. Be transparent about extra costs for windows or pest control. After the walkthrough, send a written quote within 24 hours. If the client seems hesitant, offer a trial clean at a 20% discount. Always follow up with a thank-you message. This personal touch sets you apart from competitors who just send a price via text.

lessons.title: Writing and Presenting Service Proposals
lessons.body: A service proposal is a document that outlines what you will do, how, and for how much. For small residential clients, a WhatsApp message can work, but for commercial clients, a formal PDF is better. Use free tools like Canva or Google Docs to create a professional template. Include: your business name and logo, client name and address, date, scope of work (e.g., 'Weekly cleaning of 5 offices, 2 restrooms, and kitchenette'), frequency, duration per visit, list of tasks (vacuuming, mopping, dusting, sanitizing), equipment and products you will use, total monthly cost, payment terms (e.g., 50% deposit, balance on completion), and validity of quote (30 days). For example, a proposal for a 200 sqm office in Lagos might be NGN 80,000 per month for weekly cleaning. Present the proposal in person or via a video call. Walk them through each section, highlighting benefits: 'This will keep your staff healthy and your office presentable.' Address concerns about security: 'All our staff are vetted and insured.' Ask for the sale: 'Can we start next Monday?' If they need time, schedule a follow-up. Always send a thank-you email after presenting. Keep a copy for your records. A good proposal reduces misunderstandings and makes you look professional.

lessons.title: Negotiating Contracts with Commercial Clients
lessons.body: Commercial clientsâoffices, schools, hospitalsâoffer steady income but they negotiate hard. Before meeting, know your costs: labor, transport, supplies, and profit margin. For example, if you pay a cleaner KES 500 per day and need 3 cleaners for a 5-day week, labor is KES 7,500 per week. Add 20% for supplies and 30% profit. So your minimum weekly price is about KES 12,000. Never go below this. When negotiating, focus on value, not price: 'Our team is trained and insured, so you avoid liability.' Offer tiered packages: basic, standard, premium. For a 12-month contract, offer a 10% discount. Ask for a 3-month trial period. If they push for a lower price, reduce frequency or scope, not your rate. For example, 'We can do fortnightly instead of weekly for KES 8,000.' Always get the agreement in writing, signed by both parties. Include termination clause (30 days notice), payment terms (invoice on 1st, due on 15th), and penalties for late payment. Use a simple contract template from LawDepot or a local lawyer. Build rapport: small talk, remember names, send birthday wishes. Commercial clients value reliability over cheapness. Deliver excellent service, and they will renew.

lessons.title: Using CRM Software to Manage Client Interactions
lessons.body: CRM stands for Customer Relationship Management. It helps you track leads, clients, and communications. For a small cleaning business, free tools are enough. Start with Google Contacts and Google Sheets: create columns for Name, Phone, Email, Address, Service Type, Last Contact, Next Follow-up, Notes. Or use HubSpot CRM (free) which lets you log calls, emails, and set reminders. For WhatsApp-based businesses, use WhatsApp Business App: label chats (New Lead, Client, Follow-up), set quick replies, and use broadcast lists for promotions. For example, after a cleaning, send a follow-up message: 'How was our service? Please leave a review.' Set reminders to contact commercial clients monthly. Track your conversion rate: if you get 20 leads and 5 become clients, that's 25%. Use CRM to segment clients: residential vs commercial, one-time vs recurring. Send seasonal offers: 'Deep clean before Christmas at 15% off.' For invoicing, use Wave or Zoho Invoice (free). Keep all client data secureâdon't share phone numbers. A CRM saves time and helps you remember important details, like a client's preference for unscented detergents. Train your staff to update the CRM after every job. This system turns one-time clients into repeat customers.

lessons.title: Building Long-Term Relationships and Reducing Churn
lessons.body: Churn is when clients stop using your service. To reduce churn, focus on reliability and communication. Always arrive on time, do a thorough job, and leave a checklist of what was done. After each cleaning, ask for feedback: 'Is there anything we missed?' If a client complains, fix it within 24 hoursâoffer a free re-clean. Send monthly newsletters via WhatsApp or email with cleaning tips: 'How to remove coffee stains.' Celebrate milestones: 'Happy 1 year with us! Here's a 10% discount on your next deep clean.' For commercial clients, schedule quarterly reviews to discuss performance and adjust scope. Offer loyalty rewards: after 10 cleanings, one is free. Build personal connections: remember names of staff, bring small gifts during holidays. Use a CRM to track birthdays and anniversaries. When a client cancels, ask why and try to win them back with a special offer. Survey your clients every 6 months using Google Forms. If churn is high, analyze: are your prices too high? Is quality inconsistent? Train your team regularly. Aim to retain 80% of clients annually. A happy client refers othersâword of mouth is the cheapest marketing. Treat every client like your only client, and they will stay for years.

quiz.q: What is the recommended maximum response time for a new inquiry during business hours?

quiz.q: What is a good tool to create a professional proposal?

quiz.q: When negotiating with commercial clients, what should you focus on?
quiz.explanation: Commercial clients value reliability and quality over the cheapest price.

options: D) No payment until end of year

quiz.q: What does CRM stand for?

quiz.q: What feature in WhatsApp Business helps manage client interactions?

quiz.q: How often should you follow up with commercial clients according to the CRM lesson?

quiz.q: What is churn?

quiz.explanation: Fixing complaints quickly shows you care and can retain the client.

quiz.q: What is a loyalty reward mentioned in the lesson?

quiz.q: How can you reduce churn?
options: B) Offer discounts for long-term contracts

quiz.explanation: Monthly newsletters with tips keep your business top-of-mind without being spammy.

quiz.explanation: CRM helps track leads, communications, and follow-ups efficiently.

options: A) It attracts them to try your service
